events.what: Self-published GitHub repository reports computational verification of Grimm's conjecture up to 10^12 (previous published bound 1.9×10^10, Laishram & Shorey 2006)
events.credibility_reason: Pseudonymous self-published repository, no expert uptake; erdosproblems.com still cites only the 2006 bound.

events.what: Lean 4 certificate of Grimm's conjecture on the finite range [2, 10^4], submitted to the Justin Sun Prize and rejected as not a full solution

judgement.doubts: Both events check finitely many instances of a universal statement (F4); neither can move the status. The CLAUDE.md in the repository hints at AI-agent-written code, but that is irrelevant once the event is discarded as instances, and writing verification code would not be mathematics in any case.

corrections.why: F4: the record itself says extending the search range 'narrows where a counterexample could hide but does not settle the conjecture'. Checking up to 10^12 (and the Lean certificate on [2,10^4]) is scope instances, which is not movement, so no event survives.
F4: once the finite-verification events are discarded, the record shows no post-snapshot movement on the bullet.
